C. N-(4-amino-5-cyano-6-ethoxy-2-pyridinyl)-2-(2-methoxyphenyl)acetamide

Thought: Let me break down the SMILES notation C1=CC=C(OC)C(CC(=O)NC2=CC(N)=C(C#N)C(OCC)=N2)=C1 and compare it with the given options.

The SMILES notation represents:
- C1=CC=C(OC)C(...)=C1: A benzene ring with a methoxy group (OC) and another substituent
- The substituent contains CC(=O)N: This is an acetamide group
- C2=CC(N)=C(C#N)C(OCC)=N2: A pyridine ring with amino (N), cyano (C#N), and ethoxy (OCC) groups

Looking at the options:
A. 3-[4-[(2-cyanophenyl)methoxy]phenyl]propanoic acid - This has a propanoic acid group which isn't in our SMILES
B. N-(2-chloro-5-methoxy-phenyl)-2-methyl-5-oxo-4-propyl-4,6,7,8-tetrahydro-1H-quinoline-3-carboxamide - This has a chloro group and a quinoline structure not in our SMILES
C. N-(4-amino-5-cyano-6-ethoxy-2-pyridinyl)-2-(2-methoxyphenyl)acetamide - This has a pyridine with amino, cyano, and ethoxy groups connected via an acetamide to a methoxyphenyl group, which matches our SMILES
D. tert-butyl N-[5-[5-[(2-methylphenyl)methylsulfanyl]-1,3,4-oxadiazol-2-yl]pentyl]carbamate - This has an oxadiazole structure not in our SMILES

Option C appears to match our SMILES notation. It has:
- A 2-methoxyphenyl group (the benzene with OC)
- An acetamide linker (CC(=O)N)
- A pyridine with amino, cyano, and ethoxy groups in the positions indicated by the SMILES
Final Answer: [ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
